matrix_guide.title: QR Matrix Versions & Pegboard Sizing Chart
matrix_guide.lead: Unlike standard digital QR codes, fuse bead patterns must physically align with fixed pegboard pin grids. A standard square pegboard features 29×29 pins spaced at 5.0mm centers (14.5cm × 14.5cm total). Every scannable QR code requires a strict 4-module quiet zone (white margin) on all four sides according to ISO/IEC 18004 standards.
matrix_guide.p1: Smartphone camera auto-focus and edge-detection algorithms use the quiet zone to separate the finder patterns (the three large corner squares) from the background surface. If beads touch the edge of the board without a margin, the phone sensor will fail to identify the orientation markers.
matrix_guide.row1_capacity: Up to ~17 alphanumeric chars (Short links, tiny WiFi)
matrix_guide.row2_capacity: Up to ~32 alphanumeric chars (Normal URLs, standard WiFi)
matrix_guide.row3_capacity: Up to ~53 alphanumeric chars (Detailed links, vCard)
matrix_guide.row4_capacity: Up to ~78 alphanumeric chars (Full vCard, complex URLs)
matrix_guide.pro_tip: Crafter's Golden Rule: Always use URL shorteners (such as bit.ly or tinyurl.com) or concise direct handles before generating. Keeping your payload under 20 characters locks the pattern to Version 1 (21×21), allowing the entire design and 4-bead quiet zone to fit perfectly onto a single standard 29×29 pegboard!

brand_guide.title: Fuse Bead Brand Comparison: Melting Points & Compatibility
brand_guide.lead: A functional QR code is a precision optical relief. If dark and light beads melt at different rates or collapse unevenly, micro-shadows will break camera scanning. Never mix different brands of fuse beads within the active QR matrix area.
brand_guide.card1_desc: The North American gold standard. Perler beads offer uniform wall thickness and a soft, predictable melt. Recommended codes: Solid Black #5018 (dark modules) and Solid White #5001 (light modules and quiet zone).
brand_guide.card2_desc: Artkal S-Series features a higher melting temperature and rigid plastic structure. It produces crisp, razor-sharp flat melts with zero bead warping, making it the favorite for competition-grade QR pixel art.
brand_guide.card3_desc: Hama beads melt substantially faster with thinner sidewalls. When using Hama Black 18 and White 01, keep your iron moving continuously in small circles to avoid accidentally flattening the hollow centers.
brand_guide.warning_mixing: Critical Warning: If you mix Perler and Hama beads in the same pattern, Hama beads will over-melt and slump into liquid puddles before Perler beads have fully bonded, creating distorted module heights that blind camera auto-focus.

optical_guide.title: Color Contrast & The Single-Sided Flat Melt Technique
optical_guide.lead: Smartphone QR scanners rely on binarization algorithms—converting camera pixels into absolute black or white based on a dynamic luminance threshold. Three physical factors dictate scanning success:
optical_guide.factor1_desc: Black and White delivers a 98% scan success rate across all lighting conditions. High-contrast alternatives include Midnight Blue on Buttercream Yellow, or Dark Cranberry on Ivory. Never use pastel pink on white, neon green on yellow, or dark purple on black.
optical_guide.factor2_desc: Glossy molten plastic acts as a mirror under overhead LED spotlights or sunlight. When light reflects directly into the camera lens, black beads register as bright white hotspots, corrupting data packets. Always use matte parchment paper and avoid wax paper.
optical_guide.factor3_desc: By thoroughly melting only the reverse side of the project, the beads fuse into a sturdy plastic sheet while the front display side retains distinct circular bead holes. These hollow holes absorb ambient light, providing deep physical contrast that smartphones read in milliseconds.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Why does my phone struggle to scan beaded QR codes?
faq.a1: The three most common culprits are: 1) Over-ironing causing beads to flatten and create specular glare; 2) Insufficient quiet zone (you must leave at least 4 rows of white beads around the perimeter); 3) Using translucent or low-contrast bead colors. Our Level H generator and 1:1 guide solve all three.
faq.q2: Can I use mini beads (2.6mm) instead of midi beads (5mm)?
faq.a2: Yes! The pattern grid is identical. However, with mini 2.6mm beads, the finished physical size will be roughly half as large (e.g., ~7.5cm instead of ~14.5cm for a 29×29 matrix). Ensure your phone camera can focus closely on high-density mini patterns.
faq.q3: Why is Level H (30%) error correction the default?
faq.a3: Midi beads are handcrafted and melted with heat, which introduces minor optical imperfections like hole narrowing or slight melting tilt. Level H embeds enough Reed-Solomon redundancy that up to 30% of the QR code can be distorted or covered while remaining 100% scan-ready.
faq.q4: Which side should I iron for the best scanning result?
faq.a4: We strongly recommend the 'Flat Melt' method: melt the back side until completely fused for durability, while keeping the display front side lightly melted so the bead holes remain distinct and crisp. This eliminates top glare.
faq.q5: Are my WiFi passwords or text sent to any server?
faq.a5: No! ScanBeads runs 100% locally in your web browser. Zero network requests, zero database logging, and zero tracking of your personal data.
faq.q6: What is the best ironing paper to use for scannable bead art?
faq.a6: Always use unbleached baker's parchment paper or professional silicone craft film. Never use kitchen wax paper, as the wax coating melts directly into the bead plastic, leaving a cloudy white residue that degrades optical contrast and ruins scanner readability.
faq.q7: How do I prevent my beaded QR code from warping or bending while cooling?
faq.a7: Immediately after lifting your iron, transfer the hot beaded piece (still covered in parchment paper) onto a smooth flat tabletop. Place a heavy flat weight—such as two large hardcover encyclopedias or a marble chopping board—on top for at least 15 minutes until room temperature. Flatness is essential so camera lenses can capture the entire matrix in uniform focus.

tool_guide.title: How the ScanBeads Fuse Bead QR Engine Works
tool_guide.lead: Converting digital binary code into a physical pegboard mosaic requires specialized matrix transformations and optical calibration.
tool_guide.sec1_title: 1. Reed-Solomon Error Correction for Handcrafted Art
tool_guide.sec1_desc: Unlike digital QR codes displayed on pristine smartphone screens, handcrafted fuse bead pieces endure heat variations, slight hole misalignments, and surface micro-shadows. Our generator defaults to Level H error correction (30% redundancy). This means that even if several beads melt irregularly, get scratched, or reflect overhead glare, your phone camera can mathematically reconstruct 100% of the lost payload using Reed-Solomon polynomial error correction.
tool_guide.sec2_desc: Every printable PDF generated by ScanBeads is calibrated to true 100% physical scale. Standard 5mm midi pegboard pins are manufactured at exact 5.0mm pitch intervals (center-to-center spacing). When printing the PDF, select 'Actual Size' or 'Scale: 100%' in your printer dialog (disable 'Fit to Page'). Place a clear transparent square pegboard directly on top of the printed paper; the pins will align perfectly with each colored circle, enabling rapid bead placement without manual grid counting.
tool_guide.sec3_title: 3. Brand Color Code Accuracy (Perler, Artkal, Hama)
tool_guide.sec3_desc: Not all black and white beads are created equal. Solid Black (Perler #5018 / Artkal S01 / Hama 18) provides a light absorption coefficient of over 95%, ensuring maximum contrast against Solid White (Perler #5001 / Artkal S02 / Hama 01). Always use opaque colors; never use translucent, pearl, or glow-in-the-dark beads within the active QR grid area.
tool_guide.sec4_title: 4. Pegboard Interlocking Math & Large Matrix Layouts
tool_guide.sec4_desc: When your payload exceeds Version 1 (e.g. detailed vCards or long URLs), the matrix expands to Version 2 (33×33 total beads) or Version 3 (37×37 total beads). Because a single pegboard has 29 pins, you must connect four interlocking square pegboards into a 2×2 grid (yielding a 58×58 pin workspace). Our generator highlights the exact quadrant coordinates so you know where the pattern boundary lies across the pegboard seams.
tool_guide.sec5_title: 5. Calculating Exact Bead Pack Quantities & Waste Margins
tool_guide.sec5_desc: A 29×29 bead matrix consists of 841 individual fuse beads. A typical Version 1 pattern with a 4-bead quiet zone requires approximately 480 to 520 white beads and 320 to 360 dark beads. We recommend keeping a buffer of at least 50 extra beads per color to account for dropped beads, factory mold defects, or irregular heights. Standard 1,000-bead single-color bags or 6,000-bead value jars provide more than enough supply for multiple scannable projects.
tool_guide.sec6_desc: When encoding sensitive data such as private home WiFi WPA2/WPA3 passwords or personal contact information, privacy is paramount. Unlike online QR generators that route your data through external server APIs or URL redirect trackers, ScanBeads processes all QR matrix generation and PDF rendering entirely within your browser's local JavaScript runtime. Your WiFi credentials never leave your device.
tool_guide.sec7_title: 7. Smartphone Camera Focal Distance & Optical Physics
tool_guide.sec7_desc: When testing your fuse bead QR code with iOS Camera, Google Lens, or native Android barcode scanners, camera lens focal distance is key. Standard smartphone main sensors have a minimum focusing distance of approximately 8cm to 12cm. Because a 5mm midi bead matrix produces a physical square measuring 14.5cm across (for Version 1), your camera will naturally capture the entire code from 20cm to 30cm away without requiring macro mode. If using 2.6mm mini beads, the pattern shrinks to 7.5cm; hold the device at 15cm and ensure bright, diffused lighting to prevent shadow cast from your phone body.
tool_guide.sec8_title: 8. High-Yield Batch Crafting: Coasters, Keychains & Wall Art
tool_guide.sec8_desc: Once you have perfected your first scannable piece, consider exploring functional mounting options. For tabletop WiFi stands and bar drink coasters, backing the melted bead square with self-adhesive 2mm natural cork roll provides heat insulation and non-slip stability while protecting wooden tables. For convention badges and backpack zipper pulls, install a 12mm metal split ring through a corner quiet zone hole before ironing to create a reinforced mechanical anchor that won't tear under tension.
tool_guide.sec9_title: 9. Color Theory for Decorative & Themed Pegboards
tool_guide.sec9_desc: While Classic Monochrome (Solid Black #5018 on Solid White #5001) offers the highest scanning tolerance, you can create themed patterns using dark saturated tones such as Midnight Blue (#5089), Forest Green (#5053), or Dark Plum (#5091) paired with White (#5001) or Cream (#5002). Always maintain a minimum 4:1 Weber contrast ratio: never pair medium grey with white, and avoid pastel tones for dark modules. Keep the three corner finder pattern squares solid and high-contrast.
tool_guide.sec10_desc: Never leave acrylic pegboards under direct midday sunlight, in warm car trunks, or near heating vents. Acrylic begins to soften and warp above 65°C (149°F), causing pegboard pins to tilt outwards. Store your pegboards horizontally flat in a cool, dry craft drawer with a protective cardboard divider between boards to protect pins from bending.

tutorial.title: How to Make a Perler Bead QR Code
tutorial.subtitle: Step-by-step craftsman tutorial for making scannable Perler bead QR codes. Learn the single-sided flat iron melt, quiet zone rules, and zero-glare contrast.
tutorial.sec1_p1: Every successful beaded QR code begins with payload restraint. QR matrix dimensions expand dynamically based on text length and error correction tier. For maximum ease, keep your input concise:
tutorial.sec1_point1: The 29×29 Pegboard Sweet Spot: A standard square pegboard contains 29×29 pins. A Version 1 QR code is 21×21 modules. Adding the mandatory 4-module quiet zone on all sides results in exactly 29×29 beads (21 + 4 + 4 = 29). This allows your entire scannable QR code to fit on a single pegboard without interlocking joins.
tutorial.sec1_point2: Payload Limit for Single Board: With Level H (30%) error correction, a Version 1 QR code can encode up to 17 alphanumeric characters or ~10 bytes of binary data. Use concise short links (e.g. bit.ly, tinyurl) or simple WiFi network names to stay within Version 1.
tutorial.sec1_point3: Version 2 & Beyond: If your URL or WiFi password requires 18 to 32 characters, the generator automatically steps up to Version 2 (25×25 matrix + 8 margin = 33×33 beads). This requires interlocking four 29×29 pegboards into a 2×2 grid.
tutorial.sec2_title: Stage 2: Precision Pegboard Placement & The Tape Method
tutorial.sec2_p1: Assembling the beads accurately is the second step. Follow these professional workshop practices:
tutorial.sec2_step1: 1:1 Transparent Pegboard Overlay: Print the 1:1 PDF template at 100% scale. Place your clear acrylic pegboard directly over the printed sheet. Tape the corners of the pegboard to your desk to prevent shifting while placing beads.
tutorial.sec2_step2: Use Precision Tweezers: Place dark beads into the three corner finder patterns (the 7×7 outer squares and 3×3 inner solid squares) first. These serve as visual anchors for the rest of the pattern.
tutorial.sec2_step3: The Blue Painter's Tape Method: Never iron directly on your acrylic pegboard! High heat warps plastic pegboard pins permanently. Once all beads are placed, apply strips of blue painter's tape across the entire bead surface, overlapping strips by 5mm. Smooth down firmly with an old credit card to ensure every bead adheres to the tape.
tutorial.sec2_step4: Poking Vent Holes: Gently lift the taped bead sheet off the pegboard pins. Flip it over (tape side down). Using a spare pegboard or a precision awl, poke a vent hole through the tape into every single bead cavity. This prevents trapped hot air from causing blowouts or uneven melting.
tutorial.sec3_title: Stage 3: The Single-Sided Flat Iron Melt Technique
tutorial.sec3_p1: Ironing makes or breaks optical scan reliability. Heat control is the most critical factor:
tutorial.sec3_step1: Iron Temperature Calibration: Set your domestic dry iron to Medium heat (the Wool or Cotton setting, approximately 145°C - 155°C). Ensure steam is completely turned off and empty any residual water from the iron reservoir.
tutorial.sec3_step2: Use Unbleached Parchment Paper: Lay a clean sheet of baker's parchment paper flat over the bead surface. Never use waxed paper—wax melts into the plastic pores, leaving a milky hazy residue that ruins camera contrast.
tutorial.sec3_step3: Gentle Circular Motion: Hold the iron lightly without bearing down with excessive body weight. Move in smooth, uniform 5cm circles across the matrix. Spend roughly 25 to 35 seconds across the entire piece until the bead tops gently fuse and the holes slightly narrow.
tutorial.sec3_step4: Single-Sided Fusion: Only melt this back side! Do NOT flip the piece to melt the front display side. Keeping the front bead holes open creates physical light-absorbing cavities that eliminate blinding top reflections when smartphone cameras scan the surface.
tutorial.sec4_p1: Fused plastic contracts as it cools from 150°C down to room temperature. Without pressure, the piece will curl into a curved 'taco' shape:
tutorial.sec4_tip1: Immediate Weight Application: Immediately lift the parchment-covered hot piece and slide it onto a completely flat wooden or granite surface.
tutorial.sec4_tip2: Weighted Compression: Place two heavy hardcover books or a 5kg flat weight on top. Leave undisturbed for at least 15 minutes until the plastic is cool to the touch. A dead-flat surface is mandatory for smartphone cameras to focus evenly across all four corners.
tutorial.sec5_title: Stage 5: Smartphone Camera Scanning Diagnostic & Troubleshooting
tutorial.sec5_p1: If your smartphone camera does not immediately recognize your completed piece, check these four diagnostic criteria:
tutorial.sec5_diag1: Check Lighting Angle: Direct overhead fluorescent or LED lights cause specular highlights on melted bead surfaces. Tilt the piece by 15 degrees or move to diffuse daylight to eliminate glare.
tutorial.sec5_diag2: Confirm the 4-Bead White Border: Ensure your 4-module quiet zone is intact and not placed directly on a dark tablecloth. If displayed on a dark table, mount the piece onto a white cardboard or foam backing.
tutorial.sec5_diag3: Clean Camera Lens: Wipe your phone lens with a microfiber cloth. Smudges or oils on the camera glass soften pixel contrast, preventing edge-detection filters from locking onto the corner finder squares.
tutorial.sec5_diag4: Color Purity Verification: Ensure you used pure opaque solid beads. Mixing semi-translucent or pearl beads reduces luminance contrast below the 70% threshold required by standard QR barcode scanning engines.
